The Backfire Awards

The Backfire Awards site at backfireawards.com: the feed of nominee posts and Murphys, the carousels and their Instagram exports, The Midgley and The Murphy pages, the Categoric Table, search, the guidelines and terms, the Backfire Newsletter, and the merch.

Color

The Switchback palette from the logo, on every page: navy and cream grounds, orange for the one call to action, vermilion for oops, petrol and faded teal for links and data. No browns: warm hues are never mixed into dark grounds or used as faded washes. The 1970s scenes stay as illustration only. Type stays Big Shoulders Display, IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono. Every color has a night value. The site look is still named 70s in code (html[data-look]) so saved choices keep working. Night dashboards use the seven chart colors in fixed order and a teal ramp for amounts; text on charts stays cream, color sits on marks only. Each of the ten patterns has its own color, listed in public/codebook-ui.js. Contrast is the WCAG ratio against white and against the brand dark #0a2033. Click a swatch to copy its hex.

Voice

How The Backfire Awards sounds.

For outstanding achievement in unintended consequences

The famous fixes that worked too well and created new problems, and the pattern behind each, for founders and inventors who want to see the next one coming.

The exemplar. When in doubt, match it.

Write for builders

The audience is founders and inventors: people who build fixes for a living. Choose examples a founder or inventor would recognize from their own work, and end on what the next builder can take from it. Plain words still apply. (Decided 2026-10-20; the positioning doc is in the Drive drafts folder.)

Deadpan, not snide

The joke is the award itself. The copy stays plain and factual and lets the facts carry the irony.

Credit the solution first

A nominee has to have worked. Say what problem it solved before saying what it caused.

Say what people knew

State whether the harm was knowable, unforeseeable, partly knowable or still contested, and stick to documented effects.

Judge decisions, not people

Describe the decision and its effects. Leave out motives, character and private life, and nominate only public work.

Plain words for a general reader

Explain the chemistry or policy in a sentence a reader without the background can follow, as the Midgley page does.

Prose to argue, lists to scan

Argue a nomination in sentences. Criteria, moderation rules and fields go in lists.

US English, no long dashes

Write year ranges as 1889 to 1944. Use commas, colons, periods or parentheses instead of em and en dashes.

Words we use

teardownunintended consequencesworked too wellnomineethe fixstill contestedknowable at the time

Words we avoid

villain, evil, idiotclaims about a nominee's motivesundocumented effectsprivate individuals as nominees

Known gaps

Things in the wild that do not match this kit yet, so nobody copies them as the standard.

  • There is no logo file for the full element mark: the masthead tile is drawn in HTML and CSS, and the only SVG is the favicon, which carries Mg alone.
  • The favicon sets Mg as live text in Arial Narrow, not Big Shoulders Display, and the text is not outlined, so it renders differently by platform.
  • The repository is named midgely-awards while the site, the package and the Pages project spell it Midgley.
  • The home page and Midgley page screenshots in images/ show the earlier classic look.
  • Avocado and muted rose are illustration colors; no text pairing has been measured for them.

How to use this kit

One kit, three kinds of reader. kit.json is the source; this page and tokens.css are generated from it.

People

Designers, writers and contractors open this page. Copy a color, download a logo, read the voice. It works opened straight from disk.

Agents

Agents read brand/kit.json, the same kit as data. The repo's CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md points every new session at it before any design or copy work.

The site

The site loads brand/tokens.css, or copies its values, for the brand colors and fonts as CSS custom properties.

Change the kit

Edit kit.json, then rebuild and check:

python3 ~/code/site-tools/brand/brand.py build brand python3 ~/code/site-tools/brand/brand.py check brand --site public
The Backfire Awards brand kit, generated from kit.json by site-tools/brand/brand.py. Do not edit this page by hand.
